name: Multi-Helix Architecture
description: Cognition model with simultaneous processing strands — mental, emotional, physical, spiritual — producing emergent intelligence through cross-strand coupling. Each helix carries its own frequency while resonating with adjacent strands at φ-ratios. Swarm extension enables distributed multi-helix networks across parallel agents.

core_attributes.pattern: multi-strand parallel processing, cross-helix coupling, emergent cognition

scope.definition: Mutual information reduction between simultaneously-processed information strands in a multi-helix architecture — fraction of inter-strand correlation eliminated by geometric separation.

evidence.source: Watson & Crick (1953) 'A structure for deoxyribose nucleic acid', Nature 171:737-738; Pauling (1951) alpha-helix structure.
cross_domain_examples: DNA double helix: base-pair specific binding + geometric backbone separation enables independent strand readout
collagen triple helix: three parallel strands achieve tensile strength impossible for single strand — geometric synergy
RNA G-quadruplex: four-strand helix provides structural scaffold for telomere protection — 4-helix architecture

scope.falsifiability: If DNA transcription in vitro shows strand interaction rates identical for double-helix vs linear duplex, geometric helix structure does not provide strand separation advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Inter-strand separation depends on helix pitch and strand charge repulsion. Multi-helix processing advantage is architectural; actual computation independence depends on molecular recognition specificity.
